title: Psychosocial Development (Erikson)
summary: Erikson's eight stages of psychosocial development across the lifespan: trust vs mistrust, autonomy vs shame and doubt, initiative vs guilt, industry vs inferiority, identity vs role confusion, intimacy vs isolation, generativity vs stagnation, integrity vs despair.
objectives: Describe Erikson's eight stages of psychosocial development.
Identify the crisis, age and virtue of each stage.
Explain identity vs role confusion and integrity vs despair.
revision: Erikson's eight psychosocial stages across the lifespan, with crises and virtues.
traps: Erikson: 8 stages from Trust vs Mistrust (infancy) to Integrity vs Despair (late adulthood).
Each stage has a crisis and a virtue.

notes.t: Development through eight stages across the lifespan, each presenting a psychosocial crisis to resolve.
Successful resolution of each crisis produces a virtue; failure leads to difficulties in later stages.
Adolescents explore who they are; failure produces confusion about identity and role.
Older adults reflect on life; satisfaction produces integrity, regret produces despair.
UGC NET frequently asks about all eight Erikson stages, their ages, crises and virtues.

mnemonics.title: TAIIGIGI
mnemonics.text: T — Trust vs Mistrust, A — Autonomy vs Shame, I — Initiative vs Guilt, I — Industry vs Inferiority, G — Identity vs Role Confusion, I — Intimacy vs Isolation, G — Generativity vs Stagnation, I — Integrity vs Despair

flashcards.a: Trust, Autonomy, Initiative, Industry, Identity, Intimacy, Generativity, Integrity.
